topic:
Complete audit-bundle identification after locally informative monotone dropout. For every integer T>=2, specified finite alphabets W,A,X1,...,XT (A has at least two levels; Xi at least two), and specified parent sets S_t subset of {t-1,t,t+1} intersect {1,...,T}, consider causally sufficient Markovian SCMs with substantive law p(w)p(a|w)p(x1|w,a) product_{t=2}^T p(xt|w,a,x_{t-1}). All substantive tables are strictly positive. Response R0=1, R_t=R_{t-1} C_t; conditional on all substantive variables, independent response noises give q_t=P(C_t=1|w,a,x_{S_t}) in (0,1). Thus the missingness DAG has R_{t-1}->R_t and Xj->R_t exactly as allowed by S_t, with no response-to-substantive arrows and no other latent common causes. Null effects on allowed arrows are permitted. D=sum_t R_t is the final routinely observed visit. Original data are H_D=(W,A,D,X1,...,X_D). The design specifies one fixed bundle B_d subset {d+1,...,T} for each d<T. A known randomized second-stage indicator Z has P(Z=1|all substantive variables,D=d)=e_d(H_d) in (0,1), with exact recovery of X_{B_d} when Z=1; it changes no substantive variable. At D=T set Z=0. Observed datum O=(H_D,Z,X_{B_D} if Z=1), with missing symbols elsewhere. For a in A and x in X_T the target is Q_a(x)=sum_{w,x1,...,x_{T-1}} p(w) product_{t=1}^T p(xt|w,a,x_{t-1}), where t=1 omits x0. This is P(X_T=x|do(A=a)). No shadow-variable rank, parametric selection, MAR, or faithfulness assumptions are made.

Determine and prove an explicit necessary-and-sufficient criterion C(T,(S_t),(B_d),alphabet sizes) for graphwise identification of the entire vector (Q_a(x))_{a,x}. Precisely, C holds iff for every pair P,Pprime in the stated positive finite SCM class using the same known e_d, equality of their laws of O implies Q_a^P(x)=Q_a^{Pprime}(x) for every a,x. The theorem must be constructively complete: on C, output an evaluable reconstruction from the observed pattern tables valid for every compatible positive law; on failure, output two legal positive finite SCM laws with identical O laws and a different endpoint intervention probability. Provide an explicit obstruction/recovery characterization in graph and audit-pattern structure rather than generic semialgebraic decidability. From the criterion enumerate all inclusion-minimal sufficient designs B, where B<=Bprime means B_d subset Bprime_d for all d; this finite family is the focal design frontier. The exact obstruction family and reconstruction algebra are answer-open. Prove the criterion for arbitrary T in this local-parent class, not merely an exhaustive finite-T catalog. Supply consistent finite-table estimation from the reconstruction on its regular identified strata and valid projected confidence sets as described below.

Computation and inference: Known audit randomization identifies each table p(w,a,D=d,x1:d,x_{B_d}) by Horvitz–Thompson weighting, including the routine B_d=empty table. Start with these tables and derive support-aware graph/pattern elimination rules; candidate proof search combines local conditional-kernel normalization with propagation along the outcome chain. A complete graph obstruction is the missing theorem. Once supplied, test all finitely many designs (at most 2^{T(T+1)/2}) and retain inclusion-minimal successes. No polynomial complexity is claimed. Finite polynomial constraints provide only a bounded verification oracle for examples, not the headline algorithm. SCM constructive decision/reconstruction is mandatory. For iid O records, empirical observed-cell frequencies or known-e inverse-probability audit tables feed the successful reconstruction. Derive consistency, and a delta-method limit wherever the returned identifying map is differentiable with finite derivative on the positive model. For global validity, let m be the finite observed alphabet size and epsilon_n=sqrt(log(2m/alpha)/(2n)); intersect the observed-cell cube around empirical frequencies with the model image, then project compatible laws to Q (use closure of this projected set). Hoeffding plus a union bound supplies coverage >=1-alpha for all n and all legal laws; computation is finite constrained polynomial optimization. This generic coverage rung is supporting, not the field claim.

Grounding and exclusions: Theorem 6 / Appendix B: swapping gamma and 1-gamma changes the hidden marginal while preserving every routine observed record because the distinguishing variable is summed out whenever the first indicator is zero. An audit that reveals that variable in that stratum destroys that cancellation. Theorems 3–5 / Appendix A: replace recovery by setting indicators to one with recovery from an identified audit-pattern marginal before normalization. Neither step transfers verbatim, since a bundle can leave other parents and the outcome unobserved. Closest mathematical anchor: Tikka–Karvanen 2411.03848 Thms 1–6; ours has added same-subject partial-audit information and asks a complete design frontier within local Markov chains. Closest second-stage method: Levis et al. 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11639654/; their general-coarsening theorem relies on intensive follow-up recovering complete data, while our witness never recovers the full trajectory or missing endpoint. Sun et al., Estimating weighted quantile treatment effects with missing outcome data by double sampling, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11973573/, likewise assumes complete outcome recovery in the sampled subgroup (Assumptions 1–2). Yang et al. 2504.19527 identifies long-term effects under a sequential-missingness restriction, rather than deciding partial-audit sufficiency under local MNAR hazards. Primary searches on exact title/arXiv ID, self-censoring path, monotone missingness + recontact/double sampling, and authors latest publication lists returned the anchor TMLR publication and 2026 presentation, but no verified post-anchor complete audit criterion; absence is not proof of novelty. Collision snapshot only: avoid scm_threeitem_mnar_hybrid_complete (passive three-item recovery), scm_observedcsi_hedge_complete (generic observed-context CSI), and scm_selection_externalmargin_complete_id (external unbiased margin). No failed/downgraded run contents read.

Consumer: Koffman et al., Investigating Bias from Missing Data in an Electronic Health Records-Based Study of Weight Loss After Bariatric Surgery, Obesity Surgery 2021, DOI 10.1007/s11695-021-05226-y, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33462670/: 2,883 surgery patients, recontact survey among disenrollees, five-year weight distributions. The result would let analogous longitudinal EHR studies determine which historical chart/survey measurements among dropout strata suffice for the five-year surgery contrast, including when recovering every missing visit or the endpoint itself is unnecessary or indispensable under a stated local DAG. It does not claim their existing self-selected survey is randomized. Geng et al., Tropical Medicine & International Health 2010, DOI 10.1111/j.1365-3156.2010.02507.x, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20586962/, is a second concrete tracing consumer: the sampling-corrected HIV mortality determinants changed, motivating sufficient-measurement protocols.

PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The presolver derived an arbitrary-horizon minimal-audit frontier for one informative current/lead-parent hazard, a strictly concave two-visit reconstruction that remains unique at deficient rank, and a binary-versus-larger intermediate-alphabet boundary for a specified three-visit remote-audit graph. Exact enumeration reproduced the original witness with positive audit coins even for empty bundles. A new four-visit overlapping-bundle pair matches all 138 positive observed cells but has endpoint probabilities one half and 119/250; a ternary intermediate pair matches 62 positive cells but gives 31/75 and 157/375. Single-hazard reconstruction was checked at 104 legal singleton positions across horizons two through five. These examples defeat simple path and normalization criteria; they do not refute the proposed full theorem. Primary-source checks, including Guo–Nabi 2026, found no verified collision with monotone partial-audit completeness.
UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Specify and prove the complete arbitrary-horizon interval-block recovery/obstruction alternative, covering parent interactions, every positive rank stratum, endpoint-only cancellations, and positive countermodel gluing.
EARLY KILL TEST: The first explicit rule system must accept the derived complementary-audit and binary-bridge cases and reject the four-visit counterexample. Then compare all 1024 designs of that fixed graph with bounded exact checks. Stop any unsound rule system; this exhaustive catalog has not yet been run.

open_problems.open_problem: Give an arbitrary-horizon necessary-and-sufficient graph-and-audit-pattern criterion for identifying every endpoint intervention distribution under locally informative monotone dropout, with constructive recovery on success and positive observationally equivalent SCM witnesses on failure.

source_refs.claim: Monotonicity can restore full-law identification in colluder structures and destroy it under mediated self-censoring; a complete characterization of target-law identification remains open.
source_refs.author: Santtu Tikka and Juha Karvanen

source_refs.claim: Randomized intensive follow-up identifies smooth complete-data functionals when follow-up recovers the complete record, but not when it reveals only a fixed partial trajectory bundle.
source_refs.author: Alexander W. Levis, Rajarshi Mukherjee, Rui Wang, Heidi Fischer, and Sebastien Haneuse

source_refs.claim: Categorical missing-data recovery can depend on observable-kernel ranks and alphabet cardinalities, so graph structure alone need not determine recoverability.
source_refs.author: Santtu Tikka and Juha Karvanen

source_refs.excerpt: Classify the determinant-zero positive stratum of residual case 6 and construct accepted certificates for all strata
A positive local contrast can disappear after global contraction.
prove a transfer lemma from an IDSB/EXT-ID terminal obstruction to a graph-compatible response-fiber construction

open_problems.why_unsolved: Passive monotone-MNAR recovery normalizes kernels using compatible all-observed response patterns, while existing double-sampling theory replaces missing records with complete trajectories. A partial audit may reveal one hazard parent while leaving another parent or the endpoint latent, so neither operation transfers directly. Prior CausalSmith runs additionally show that locally valid recovery contrasts may disappear under global contraction and that a sound recovery recursion does not automatically turn every terminal failure into a graph-compatible positive countermodel. The missing step is therefore an interval-block elimination and gluing theory that simultaneously respects the substantive Markov factorization, local hazards, all dropout-indexed audit margins, positivity, and endpoint contraction.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite interval-block obstruction/recovery theorem that decides every local-parent graph and bundle family, returns an evaluable reconstruction of all Q_a(x) on success, and compiles every terminal obstruction into two strictly positive finite SCMs with identical observed audit laws and unequal endpoint probabilities.

writing_exemplar.why: Its blessing-versus-curse framing motivates a complete identification boundary rather than another sufficient condition.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Monotone dropout appears simpler than unrestricted missingness -> monotonicity changes which recovery operations are valid -> it can create or destroy identification -> randomized partial audits require a complete recovery-or-obstruction criterion

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt response-kernel recovery by fixing compatible indicators to one and the positive gamma-swap nonidentification construction, replacing routine all-observed marginals with identified audit-pattern marginals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies both constructive recovery and positive observational-equivalence arguments for monotone response mechanisms.

method_exemplars.technique: Generalize its conditional-kernel matrix equations and rank-sensitive necessity arguments from one categorical colluder block to overlapping interval audit blocks.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired criterion must remain correct across finite alphabet sizes and nongeneric positive rank strata.

method_exemplars.technique: Use known second-stage probabilities to estimate audit-pattern tables and transform the derivative of the recovered Q functional into an observed-data influence function.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides the nearest estimator and limit-theory machinery for randomized follow-up, differing at the complete-record recovery step.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the alphabet- and rank-stratified boundary at which positive partial-audit tables identify an endpoint effect through rational normalization, through a uniquely isolated algebraic root, or not at all.

source_refs.claim: Finite categorical missing-data identification can change with alphabet size and rank, including binary-versus-larger-alphabet distinctions.
source_refs.author: Santtu Tikka and Juha Karvanen

source_refs.excerpt: an injective map can have only a non-rational algebraic inverse
including an explicit test for a non-rational algebraic inverse

open_problems.why_unsolved: Strict positivity does not imply the full-rank conditions used by matrix-normalization arguments. Binary intermediate states may impose normalization identities that disappear for larger alphabets, while a deficient-rank observed map may still determine Q through a unique nonlinear root. The earlier three-item project explicitly left open the distinction between rational inversion, non-rational injectivity, and a genuinely target-varying positive fiber. The required first step is an exact support-and-minor stratification of the audit observation map, followed by real-algebraic branch control rather than a generic-rank argument.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite support-and-rank stratification theorem assigning every positive stratum either an explicit rational reconstruction, a uniquely isolated real-root reconstruction with a branch certificate, or two positive algebraic SCM points in one observed fiber with unequal Q.

writing_exemplar.why: It treats categorical cardinality and observable-kernel rank as first-class determinants of identification.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Finite MNAR models induce polynomial observation maps -> graphical criteria can miss alphabet-sensitive behavior -> generic rank omits legal singular positive laws -> partial-audit identification needs an exact algebraic stratum classification

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over colluder-matrix equations and their cardinality-sensitive rank analysis, replacing a single matrix inverse with blockwise elimination and isolated-root tests.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It exhibits the same finite-alphabet rank phenomenon that the proposed audit classification must resolve.

method_exemplars.technique: Encode observed-law fibers and Q separation as polynomial constraints, using exact optimization to certify isolated fibers or construct target-varying ones on bounded instances.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its polynomial representation retains nongeneric finite discrete fibers, providing a verifier for the proposed symbolic trichotomy.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine inverse audit-probability table estimation with implicit differentiation of a regular isolated branch to obtain a plug-in or one-step limit law.
method_exemplars.why_closest: On regular algebraic branches, the recovered endpoint law is a smooth functional of randomized audit-pattern probabilities.

open_problems.open_problem: For every audit-bundle design that fails point identification, characterize the sharp identified set of each endpoint probability Q_a(x) under the positive local Markov and monotone-hazard restrictions.

source_refs.claim: Discrete causal queries with incomplete or nonresponse data can be sharply bounded through polynomial optimization, but the method does not give an arbitrary-horizon graph-specific analytic recursion.
source_refs.author: Guilherme Duarte, Noam Finkelstein, Dean Knox, Jonathan Mummolo, and Ilya Shpitser
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: The mediated self-censoring construction proves nonidentification by preserving the observed law while changing a hidden distribution, but does not characterize sharp endpoint-query regions after partial audits.
source_refs.author: Santtu Tikka and Juha Karvanen

source_refs.claim: Partial identification is developed for categorical nonignorable missing outcomes under instruments and directional restrictions, not longitudinal local-hazard models with partial audits.
source_refs.author: Daniel Daly-Grafstein and Paul Gustafson

open_problems.why_unsolved: A two-law witness establishes only that an insufficient design has a non-singleton identified set. Generic polynomial optimization can bound a fixed finite instance, but it does not reveal how local transition factorization, deterministic monotone response logic, audit bundles, positivity, and arbitrary horizon determine analytic extrema. The first proof step that must change is the unrestricted response-function reduction: it must be replaced by interval-block factor elimination that preserves the local Markov model and certifies attainability, or closure-attainability, by positive SCMs.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A recursive graph-indexed formula or finite optimization with an analytic sharpness proof for the lower and upper endpoints of every Q_a(x), together with positive SCM constructions attaining those endpoints or their closure for each insufficient design.

writing_exemplar.why: Its transition from failed point identification to the sharpest data-compatible region is the appropriate motivation arc.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Credible assumptions may not point-identify a causal query -> the observed law still restricts it -> discrete causal models permit sharp optimization -> insufficient audit designs call for graph-explicit endpoint bounds

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt polynomial encodings of observed evidence and causal targets, then exploit local-chain factorization to replace black-box branch-and-bound with a symbolic interval recursion.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems seek exact ranges of a discrete causal functional under incomplete observations.

method_exemplars.technique: Generalize the paper's probability swap into a parameterized positive family whose endpoint functional traces the candidate bound while all audited margins remain fixed.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its witness already provides the local cancellation mechanism needed for a sharpness construction.

method_exemplars.technique: Express the finite audit-table restrictions as studentized sample constraints and apply calibrated projection inference to Q or to the bound endpoints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The endpoint probability is a projection of a finite-dimensional set defined by observed-table equalities and inequalities.

open_problems.open_problem: On sufficient audit designs, characterize the regular and singular strata of the identifying map and derive efficient inference for the full Q vector that remains valid as categorical elimination blocks approach or attain deficient rank.

source_refs.claim: When intensive follow-up recovers complete data, full-data influence functions can be transformed into efficient and robust observed-data estimators.
source_refs.author: Alexander W. Levis, Rajarshi Mukherjee, Rui Wang, Heidi Fischer, and Sebastien Haneuse

source_refs.claim: Categorical missing-data recovery is controlled by observable-kernel matrix ranks, and direct finite-sample equation solutions need not remain valid probability tables.
source_refs.author: Santtu Tikka and Juha Karvanen

source_refs.claim: Efficiency bounds and augmented inverse-probability estimators are available for a nonmonotone no-self-censoring model, but not for deterministic monotone dropout with partial audits and rank-changing reconstruction.
source_refs.author: Daniel Malinsky, Ilya Shpitser, and Eric J. Tchetgen Tchetgen
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

open_problems.why_unsolved: Complete-follow-up influence-function theory conditions on an audited full record, whereas a partial bundle leaves latent coordinates even in phase two. Its coarsened-data projection is therefore unavailable until the audit-pattern elimination map is differentiated. Because null allowed-arrow effects remain legal, the relevant finite matrices can lose rank within the positive model, causing ordinary derivatives to diverge or become nonunique. The first changed proof step is a tangent-space calculation through an implicit, rank-stratified identification system rather than projection of a known complete-data influence function.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A rank-stratification theorem giving the Jacobian and efficient influence function for Q on each regular identified stratum, a finite-table plug-in or one-step estimator with a joint Gaussian limit there, and a uniformly valid projected confidence set across singular and near-singular strata.

writing_exemplar.why: It clearly separates identification supplied by randomized follow-up from efficiency and robustness of the resulting causal estimator.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Informative dropout defeats routine causal analysis -> randomized follow-up supplies design-controlled information -> complete recovery supports efficient inference -> partial recovery requires rank-aware influence-function theory

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt inverse audit-probability weighting, sample splitting, and full-to-observed influence-function transformation after replacing complete-data conditioning by the derivative of the partial-audit reconstruction.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest randomized-follow-up limit theory for smooth causal functionals.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its odds-ratio tangent-space projection and augmented estimating equations to deterministic monotonicity and audited-pattern nuisance restrictions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It derives efficiency under graphical MNAR rather than ordinary MAR.

method_exemplars.technique: Use categorical kernel equations to expose exact rank strata, then apply implicit differentiation or generalized-inverse analysis to overlapping bundle equations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It identifies the finite-alphabet rank phenomenon that separates regular from singular audit reconstructions.

open_problems.open_problem: Conditional on point identification being attainable, determine cost-constrained history-dependent audit probabilities and bundle choices that optimally estimate a declared scalarization of the endpoint intervention vector.

source_refs.claim: Using available EHR information to allocate double-sampling resources is identified as a future direction, while the developed estimators assume complete recovery in followed subjects.
source_refs.author: Alexander W. Levis, Rajarshi Mukherjee, Rui Wang, Heidi Fischer, and Sebastien Haneuse

source_refs.claim: Optimal two-phase sampling can minimize semiparametric efficiency bounds when an expensive covariate is completely measured at phase two, but partial MNAR trajectory bundles are not covered.
source_refs.author: Ran Tao, Donglin Zeng, and Dan-Yu Lin
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Jointly optimal phase-two sampling and efficient estimation have been studied when the expensive endpoint is fully obtained for sampled subjects.
source_refs.author: Peter B. Gilbert, Xuesong Yu, and Andrea Rotnitzky

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing two-phase design results allocate complete endpoint or expensive-covariate measurements using a previously derived influence-function variance contribution. With partial audits, bundle choice first changes whether Q is identified and then changes the derivative and efficiency bound of its nonlinear reconstruction. The standard first step—writing variance as a separable function of inclusion probabilities—must therefore be rederived jointly with a discrete identification constraint over admissible bundle families.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An identification-constrained optimization theorem giving an optimal bundle family and measurable probabilities e_d^*(H_d) under a stated budget and loss such as trace or worst-coordinate asymptotic variance, plus a consistent pilot-adaptive implementation and the resulting limit law for Q.

writing_exemplar.why: Its study-design framing and resource-allocation direction provide the closest destination narrative without suggesting that it already handles partial bundles.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Informative longitudinal dropout threatens causal inference -> randomized follow-up restores investigator-controlled information -> follow-up measurements are costly -> choose partial bundles and sampling probabilities that retain identification and maximize precision

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt efficiency-bound minimization and residual-dependent sampling rules, replacing a single expensive-variable inclusion probability with dropout-history-specific probabilities indexed by discrete bundle choices.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It directly couples phase-two sampling design to a semiparametric efficiency bound.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over budget-constrained Neyman allocation based on conditional influence-function variability and its pilot plug-in implementation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its complete phase-two endpoint-recovery design is the closest analogue of allocating costly post-dropout audit information.

method_exemplars.technique: Use its randomized-follow-up influence function to express how history-dependent audit probabilities enter asymptotic variance after substituting a partial-bundle influence function.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It connects MNAR causal estimation, investigator-controlled sampling probabilities, and efficiency in the same application regime.

literature_map:
Tikka and Karvanen (2025, TMLR, arXiv:2411.03848) show that monotonicity can rescue colluder models yet create nonidentification under mediated self-censoring, and leave complete target-law characterization open.
Nabi, Bhattacharya, and Shpitser (2020, ICML, arXiv:2004.04872) give a complete full-law criterion for ordinary missing-data DAGs, but not deterministic monotone response logic.
Bhattacharya, Nabi, Shpitser, and Robins (2019, UAI, arXiv:1907.00241) emphasize that target-law recovery can succeed even when the full law is unrecoverable.
Mohan and Pearl (2021, JASA, DOI 10.1080/01621459.2021.1874961) organize graphical missing-data work around recoverability and testability, without randomized partial post-dropout audits.
Guo and Nabi (2026, arXiv:2602.10969) give a constructive intervention tree for tracking selection-bias propagation, but no monotone partial-bundle frontier.
Tikka and Karvanen (2024, arXiv:2402.05633) prove alphabet- and rank-sensitive categorical recovery, including binary-versus-larger-alphabet changes.
Karvanen and Tikka (2024, arXiv:2410.18688) distinguish target-law from full-law identification and study factorizable imputation rather than partial audits.
Levis et al. (2024, Statistics in Medicine, arXiv:2204.02432) identify smooth complete-data functionals and derive efficient estimators when randomized intensive follow-up recovers complete data.
Sun et al. (2025, Biometrics, arXiv:2310.09239) obtain weighted-quantile treatment-effect inference by double sampling that recovers the missing outcome in sampled subjects.
Yang et al. (2025, arXiv:2504.19527) identify long-term effects under a sequential-missingness restriction rather than deciding partial-audit sufficiency under local MNAR hazards.
Malinsky, Shpitser, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2023, JASA, arXiv:1909.01848) derive efficiency theory under nonmonotone no-self-censoring, offering adjacent MNAR inference machinery.
Duarte et al. (2024, JASA, arXiv:2109.13471) reduce discrete causal problems with incomplete data to polynomial optimization for sharp numerical bounds, useful as a bounded oracle rather than an arbitrary-T structural theorem.
Daly-Grafstein and Gustafson (2026, Canadian Journal of Statistics, DOI 10.1002/cjs.70037) study partial identification for categorical nonignorable missing outcomes under additional restrictions, not longitudinal partial audits.
Tao, Zeng, and Lin (2020, JASA) and Gilbert, Yu, and Rotnitzky (2014, Statistics in Medicine) optimize phase-two sampling when sampled subjects yield the complete expensive variable.
Exact-title, partial-follow-up, monotone-MNAR, audit-bundle, and author-publication searches found no verified complete arbitrary-horizon criterion with fixed partial bundles; this search result is not proof of novelty.
